weaknesses: The central theoretical argument is not sound as stated. The Fourier derivative result requires integrability, decay, and boundary assumptions that are omitted; continuity of higher derivatives alone does not imply the claimed spectral decay. Moreover, ReLU and GELU are not integrable over the real line as ordinary functions. Most importantly, the Fourier transform of an activation as a scalar function of its argument does not directly characterize the spatial-frequency spectrum of the composed feature map σ(x(t)).

The convolution theorem only establishes that multiplication can alter or enlarge spectral support. It does not show that a gate learns useful high-frequency information, improves classification, or avoids noise. For discrete feature maps the relevant operation is circular convolution with possible aliasing, which is not considered. Thus the theory does not support the paper's main causal interpretation.

The frequency evaluation is inadequately defined: θ(z;R), mask geometry, inverse transformation, normalization, and treatment of complex values are unspecified. Accuracy on frequency-filtered test images is also an out-of-distribution proxy confounded by overall model accuracy and filtering artifacts; it is not direct evidence about internal frequency learning or training dynamics.

The architectural novelty is limited to a simple self-gating operation combined with familiar depthwise and pointwise convolutions. The paper lacks a clean, parameter- and compute-matched ablation that separates the effects of gating, 7×7 depthwise convolutions, depth/width choices, and training recipe, so GmNet's gains cannot be attributed to the proposed frequency rationale.

The accuracy/latency comparison is not sufficiently controlled. Baseline accuracies appear to come from heterogeneous published recipes, while crucial latency details—batch size, precision, warm-up, repetitions, runtime versions, compilation, and operator fusion—are absent. Several claimed downstream and supplementary experiments are not included in the provided manuscript.

Reproducibility and statistical support are insufficient: augmentation, regularization, learning-rate schedule, weight decay, seeds, training hardware/time, and code are missing; main ImageNet results have no repeated-run uncertainty; and “average of five testings” is ambiguous. The proposed convolution-kernel bandwidth statistic is not mathematically defined.

The checklist asserts complete proofs, reproducibility, statistical significance, compute disclosure, and broader-impact coverage, but the manuscript lacks the corresponding assumptions, error bars, compute accounting, and societal-impact discussion. These inconsistencies further weaken confidence in the claims.

More importantly, the Fourier-decay properties of a scalar activation σ(t) do not directly determine the spatial spectrum of the composed feature σ(x(s)); the paper conflates activation-value and spatial coordinates. ReLU, ReLU6, and GELU also do not satisfy the stated integrability assumptions without additional qualification. Thus, the claimed mechanism is at best intuition rather than an established analysis.

Accuracy on Fourier-masked input images is an indirect and heavily confounded measure of what frequencies a network learns or uses. The paper does not adequately specify inverse-FFT processing, scaling, clipping, normalization, color-channel treatment, or possible ringing/aliasing. Models also differ substantially in clean accuracy, so improved high-pass accuracy need not establish a special spectral mechanism. Controlled frequency interventions, accuracy-matched models, Fourier sensitivity analyses, and statistical uncertainty are needed.

The quantitative spectral evidence is insufficiently validated. High/low energy ratios are reported for only selected layers without uncertainty, aggregation details, or controls for spatial resolution and activation magnitude. Table 14 even contradicts the statement that GELU has the lowest ratio at every stage: at Stage 2, its reported ratio exceeds ReLU's.

Novelty is limited. The proposed gate σ(x)⊙x is effectively a pointwise self-gated/clipped-quadratic activation, while the surrounding 7×7 depthwise-convolution and pointwise-MLP block uses familiar ingredients. Its distinction from squared-ReLU/StarReLU-style activations, StarNet, and prior gated convolutional architectures is not developed rigorously enough to support the broad novelty claims.

Major numerical inconsistencies undermine confidence in the empirical claims. The introduction reports GmNet-S3 at 81.3% and claims a 4.0-point gain over EfficientFormer-L1, whereas Tables 1–2 report GmNet-S3 at 79.3%, which is only 2.1 points above the table's EfficientFormer-L1 result. Table 5 reports 79.2%, and other model-size and parameter values also vary across sections.

The efficiency comparison lacks essential protocol details such as batch size, numerical precision, ONNX execution provider, warm-up, timing repetitions, variance, CoreML compute unit, and software versions. It is also unclear whether every comparator was re-benchmarked identically. Accuracy values largely come from separately trained literature models, while GmNet uses a strong 300-epoch AdamW/RandAugment/CutMix recipe, weakening architectural attribution and the claim of avoiding strong training strategies.

Reproducibility is below the expected standard: the advertised code URL is blank, no code accompanies the manuscript, the pseudocode contains apparent errors, and several experimental definitions are missing. The PGD study omits the norm, radius, step count, step size, and restarts; “five testings” is unexplained; CUB-100 is undefined; and downstream-task training protocols and variability are absent.

The manuscript contains substantial signs of incomplete revision, including a literal “?” citation placeholder, references to “the reviewer’s advice,” stale or incorrect figure references, grammatical problems, and overstatements such as “new state-of-the-art.” Given the potentially promising empirical architecture, these issues favor Reject rather than Strong Reject, but the central explanatory claims and reported comparisons are not currently reliable enough for acceptance.
